Agencies Capital markets regulator Sebi has levied fines totalling Rs 40 lakh on four entities, including two stock brokers, for allegedly facilitating front-running trades of Axis Mutual Fund . In an order passed on Tuesday, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) imposed a penalty of Rs 10 lakh each on Woodstock Broking and its director Suresh Kanmal Jajoo and Marfatia Stock Broking and its director Nishil Surendra Marfatia. The order relates to a Sebi investigation with respect to trades executed by certain entities, which appeared to be in the nature of front-running of the trades of Axis Mutual Fund (Big Client), pursuant to certain alerts generated by the surveillance system. The investigation period was from April 1, 2021 to March 31, 2022. Sebi found that the two brokers facilitated the installation and operation of their ODIN trading terminals on a computer system used by Prijesh Kurani in Dubai, who was neither an authorised person nor a registered dealer of the brokers. Live Events In the case of Woodstock Broking, Sebi relied on WhatsApp communications, technical evidence involving IP addresses and MAC IDs, and the role of its IT personnel in facilitating remote access through AnyDesk. It also noted that Visa Capital Partners, whose trading account was used in the alleged scheme, had an account with Woodstock and that Jajoo was a partner in the firm. In Marfatia's case, the market watchdog relied on a statement from its managing director, Nishil Marfatia; WhatsApp conversations involving its IT personnel; and common MAC IDs linking the trading systems used for transactions routed through the two brokers. The regulator held that the brokers aided the execution of fraudulent trades by providing the necessary infrastructure and technical assistance, in violation of the Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices (PFUTP) Rules. The stock brokers and their directors have been directed to pay the penalty amount within 45 days of receiving the order. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! The lender had reported a loss of Rs 348.5 crore a year ago. Also, the regulator has restrained the company's former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Mohit Kumar Agarwal from the securities market for eight months, while whole-time directors Naveen Sharma and Sonali Sheikh have been prohibited for five months and one month, respectively. Besides, Sebi has imposed monetary penalties totalling Rs 88 lakh on the company and other individuals for various violations of securities market regulations. Further, the markets regulator directed Dabkara to take immediate steps to recoup the amount diverted from EKI Energy Services. Also, the regulator found that EKI had overstated expenses by Rs 26.34 crore during FY22 and FY23, resulting in an understatement of its profits. "The company diverted Rs 26.34 crore by overstating expenses during 2021-22 and 2022-23," the order said. The regulator noted that EKI had "booked fictitious expenses against services not rendered", adding that payments made against such expenses "consequently constituted diversion of EKI's funds". Also, Sebi noted that Dabkara was responsible for the continued disclosure of misstated financial information and failure to ensure proper monitoring of the company's financial reporting systems. Also, the regulator held Sharma, Sheikh, and Agarwal liable for regulatory violations. ET CONTRIBUTORS Imagine building a business, attracting investors, creating thousands of jobs and investing billions in infrastructure, only to discover that a regulatory change has fundamentally rewritten the economics of your business overnight. Your customers haven't changed, and your operations remain the same, but the rules of the game have. This is where the relationship between regulation and free markets becomes complicated. Free markets thrive on competition, innovation and commercial freedom. Regulation, on the other hand, is essential to protect consumers, prevent the misuse of market power and build trust. The challenge begins when intervention goes beyond correcting market failures and starts altering the economic incentives that make businesses viable. For investors, regulation is not merely a compliance matter; it can fundamentally change the earnings potential, valuation and long-term attractiveness of an entire industry. In September, insurance stocks came under pressure following proposed regulatory changes by IRDAI concerning commissions and distribution practices. The intention is understandable: curb mis-selling, improve transparency, reduce distribution costs and ultimately deliver better value to policyholders. However, for insurers and intermediaries, distribution economics are central to profitability. A sudden change in these economics can affect earnings visibility, business expansion and investor sentiment. What the regulator sees as consumer protection , the market initially interprets as an earnings risk. Agencies Both perspectives can be valid. Live Events Not all regulation, however, creates a conflict between business interests and consumer welfare. The government's decision to cap trade margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines is an example of intervention aimed at improving affordability and access to essential treatment. Reuters A month after RBI’s rate hike, banks start raising deposit rates as liquidity shrinks, Bank of India the latest to move Mumbai: About a month after the central bank raised policy rates for the first time in four years, domestic banks are starting to raise deposit rates-albeit marginally-as liquidity shrinks and demand for credit surges through the busy season. Bank of India (BoI) is the latest lender to raise its deposit rates which, unlike external benchmark-linked lending rates, would take time to head north despite the early-October start to the hardening cycle by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). On Monday, BoI increased its deposit rates for maturities between one and below three years by 10 to 35 basis points, becoming the second bank in the current cycle to hike rates. One basis point is 0.01 percentage point. After the hike, one year deposit less than ₹3 crore will earn 6.60% interest, up from 6.50%, while one year to less than two years will earn 6.70% interest, up from 6.50%. The bank has also introduced a special 500-day deposit, which will earn 6.85%, from 6.50% earlier. "The hike in deposit rates reflects higher cost of deposits in the system. Bulk deposit rates have gone up and the bank also has to adjust the liability profile in line with the higher interest rates," said a senior BoI executive. "On the whole, liquidity in the banking system has tightened as the advantages from the unprecedented inflows from the FCNR (B) scheme have started waning." Live Events Banking system liquidity has come off from a peak of more than ₹11 lakh crore early September to about ₹1.96 lakh crore currently as a result of bond sales and variable reverse repo auctions. The tightening in liquidity can be noticed in the higher rates banks are paying in the certificate of deposit (CD) market, which have increased to over 8% for the first time since early 2023, reflecting tighter systemic liquidity. ANI Happiest Minds Technologies has reported a 15.12 per cent increase in consolidated net profit at Rs 62.19 crore for September quarter FY27. The Bengaluru-headquartered company had posted a net profit of Rs 54.02 crore for the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing. Revenue from operations rose 12.5 per cent to Rs 645.43 crore, from Rs 573.57 crore in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, profit declined 8 per cent, while revenue rose 2.7 per cent. "Our strong results reflect the continued strength of our client relationships and our focus on disciplined execution. Enterprises are increasingly looking for partners who can bring together deep domain understanding, engineering capabilities and AI-led transformation to deliver measurable business outcomes. With the complementary capabilities that ITC Infotech brings to the table, we are excited at the potential to add further value to our customers and deepen our relationship," Joseph Anantharaju, Co-Chairman & CEO, said. Live Events The quarter's results included an exceptional charge of Rs 3.98 crore incurred towards the company's proposed merger with ITC Infotech, the filing said. ITC Infotech, a wholly-owned subsidiary of diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd , will merge with Happiest Minds Technologies to create an AI-first enterprise with a USD 1 billion turnover by FY28. As a precursor to the merger, ITC Infotech will acquire a 22.10 per cent stake from Happiest Minds promoter Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP. Following the stake purchase, Happiest Minds will be amalgamated with and into ITC Infotech. The company's headcount stood at 6,466 at the end of September, compared with 6,532 at June-end and 6,554 a year earlier. The board declared an interim dividend of Rs 3.05 per equity share of face value Rs 2 for 2026-27. The record date is November 6, and the dividend will be paid on or after November 17.
